correctness.rationale: With frequencies in R/Z, every nonzero difference has cosine at one of at most two roots of P, so the allowed differences form an inversion-symmetric set of at most four points. A triangle containing 0 has either an opposite pair or v−u in {±u,±v}, making one vertex a midpoint. For four vertices, when the allowed differences contain the involution, the pair ±u must satisfy 1/2−u=±u, giving order four. Otherwise one can use {0,u,−u,v}; order three for u is excluded by the simultaneous v±u requirements, so 2u=±v. Then the 3u difference and absence of an involution give order five. Fourier inversion on C5 makes the weights uniform; on C4, P(−1)=P(0)=0 forces precisely (1/8,1/4,1/4). Independently a five-character orthonormal basis forces 5w_j=1 by unitarity. The triangle condition is P(x)=P(2x²−1)=0. The only possible fixed cosine is −1/2, giving c=a+b. Distinct roots yield the stated normalized factorization and positivity range: the cubic numerator of c has two positive extremal values, hence one real root between −1 and −1/2, and b>0 requires x<1/2 in that range. P(1)>0 makes the minimum criterion necessary and sufficient even at a double zero. At (8,10,9)/45 the two roots are 1/4 and −7/8; rationality of the angle modulo 1 would force the rational algebraic integer 2·(1/4) to be integral. All assertions concern arbitrary real frequencies, not just torsion.
residual_risks: Finite order checks do not establish the real-circle lemma; the elementary difference argument provides that step. No nonsymmetric or other-site measure is covered.

value.rationale: The maximal family size is a natural invariant of a weighted finite Fourier space. The classification locates distinct mechanisms for the transitions and the exact exceptional nonuniform four-character point. The explicit rational-weight example draws a useful boundary: integer support and rational weights do not force rational frequency differences at a maximal incomplete family, even though full finite spectra are rational in the cited setting.
residual_risks: There is no claim of a general theorem on nonsymmetric weights, larger supports or incomplete spectrum rationality beyond the explicit scope.
